newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end sharply higher.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished sharply higher on Wednesday amid tightening liquidity following the central bank's issue of T$5 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 6.720 percent against Tuesday's 6.500 close, with 30-day commercial paper rising to 6.75 against 6.50-6.60.

Although the NCD issue comes on the heels of a day of record turnover in Taiwan's red-hot stock market, the central bank said it aimed only to absorb liquidity as an earlier T$5 billion NCD issue was maturing.
Dealers expected the central bank to continue to issue NCDs on Thursday as another earlier T$8 billion NCD issue was due to mature.
The central bank has consistently denied that its repeated issuance of the short-term instruments in recent weeks intended to take some of the fire from the sizzling stock market.
Analysts suspect otherwise, saying persistently loose liquidity has been a key factor driving a huge stock rally that has pushed the share index 25 percent higher in 1997 alone.
Some dealers said the overnight interbank rate may rise to as high as 7.00 percent on Thursday.
In the bond market, the benchmark government bond yields fell. The 10-year 86/4 bond yield was traded at 6.0775 in earlier session.
